name: Pallid Violet
lede: Pallid Violet names a pale, washed-out [[violet]] by plain modifier grammar, filed by Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature and again in the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955.

sections.title: A modifier, not a coined word
sections.body:
The name follows a fixed pattern in our library: "pallid" plus the parent hue [[violet]], meaning a faded, low-saturation version of it [1]. Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* lists the swatch on plate X, hue 59, tone f [2]. The ISCC-NBS system picked the same swatch up in its 1955 dictionary, filing it in block 198 under "R" [3]. Our library files the name as an alternate of [[pale-periwinkle|Pale Periwinkle]], which shares its exact hex [1].

The nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[pallid-blue-violet]], a touch bluer, and [[pale-wistaria-blue]], almost indistinguishable [4]. [[lavender-blue]] reads more vivid, and [[pale-mauve]] leans purpler [4]. [[wedgwood-blue]] sits further off, bluer still [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a match for this violet in just 3 of them, about 0.01 percent, rarer than 81 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [5]. A pale, low-chroma violet this specific is uncommon across the whole archive, and the small count fits that pattern rather than marking anything unusual [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment identifications [5].
